newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed, mogas up $4, fuel, CFDs down.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed, mogas up $4, fuel, CFDs down.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Tuesday as a slippage in fuel oil swaps and Brent CFDs contrasted with strong gasoline gains. Gasoil differentials were barely talked.
Gasoline values jumped $4-$4.50 on September to $201-$202 as deals were heard struck at $200 and $201. The $200 deal was accompanied by a $186 November swap trade, dealers said.
The swaps jump, contrasting with a modest $1 rise on gasoline barges, saw the September crack talked firmer around $4.95 as the fourth quarter crack was valued at $3.20-$3.30.
The Sep/Oct mogas spread was meanwhile heard bid at $10.50 as naphtha outrights rose $1 on Brent crude gains.
Heavy fuel swaps eased 50 cents a tonne but trading was thin.
September barges traded at $93.50 and October between $94.50 and $95 but traders said the slow physical market was hampering activity.
Low sulphur stayed well bid after edging slightly up against barges last week.
"We're still well bid on the high-lows," said a broker.
High sulphur cargoes continued to be sharply discounted to barges, trading at $3 a tonne below for September.
In recent years cargoes have typically traded around $1 a tonne above barges.
But a lack of cargo demand has eroded that premium and dealers see little cargo buying from power companies in the short-term.
Brent CFDs slipped a cent or two with lower outright values and remained in shallow contango.
This week talk 32 cents under October with the following three weeks at 29 cents, 27 cents and 24 cents under respectively.
An extremely dull gas oil and jet market saw values unchanged as one broker referred to "a holiday market mood."
September and October jet differentials were still placed at $18.25-$18.75 and $21.25-$21.75 respectively, the October values in line with a Monday deal at $21.50.
Gasoil crack talk was flat around $4.30-$4.35 for fourth quarter, $4.30-$4.40 for first quarter 1998 at or close to $4 for second quarter 1998.
EN590 was heard either side of $5 for September and $8.50 for fourth quarter as 0.2 diesel was valued at $1-$1.50 for September $2.50-$2.75 for the fourth quarter in a disinterested market.
